words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.tr: n. 虚假；不真实；不正确
words.ex: The falsity of his story was obvious.
words.ex_cn: 他故事的虚假性显而易见。
words.en: The quality or condition of being false; incorrectness.

words.ex: The character is fictitious and does not exist in real life.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色是虚构的，现实中不存在。
words.en: Fictitious means invented and not true or not existing.

words.ex: The company made fraudulent claims about its product.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司对其产品做出了欺诈性的声明。
words.en: A fraudulent activity is deceitful or dishonest.

words.tr: adj. 错觉的，幻影的（等于 illusional）
words.ex: The mirage was an illusionary oasis.
words.ex_cn: 海市蜃楼是一个虚幻的绿洲。
words.en: Something that is illusionary is based on or involves an illusion, and is therefore not real.

words.ex: The smile on his face was illusory.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上的微笑是虚假的。
words.en: If something is illusory, it is not real or true, although it may seem to be.

words.ex: He wore a scary mask at the Halloween party.
words.ex_cn: 他在万圣节派对上戴了一个可怕的面具。
words.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over your face to hide or protect it.

words.tr: adj. 自命不凡的；自负的；矫饰的
words.ex: He wore a fancy hat to seem pretentious.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶华丽的帽子，显得自命不凡。
words.en: If you describe something as pretentious, you mean that it is intended to seem important or significant, but you think it is not.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 蠢、笨、傻

words.ex: The tailor used a dummy to fit the new coat.
words.ex_cn: 裁缝用人体模型来试穿新外套。
words.en: A dummy is a model of a person, often used for displaying clothes or for use in tests to see how something will work or fit.

words.tr:
n. 被愚弄的人；容易受骗的人
v. 欺骗；诈骗；愚弄
words.ex: He was duped into buying a fake watch.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗去买了一块假手表。
words.en: A dupe is someone who is easily deceived or cheated, often because they are too trusting. As a verb, to dupe means to deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.tr:
adj. 文盲的；无知的；
n. 文盲；无知识的人；
words.ex: He is illiterate and cannot read simple signs.
words.ex_cn: 他是文盲，无法阅读简单的标识。
words.en: Someone who is illiterate cannot read or write.

words.ex: The loud speaker is too obtrusive.
words.ex_cn: 这个扬声器太突兀了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is obtrusive, you mean they are noticeable in an unwelcome or inappropriate way.

words.tr: adj. 钝的；愚钝的；钝角的
words.ex: The angle is obtuse, so it is larger than 90 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 这个角是钝的，所以它大于90度。
words.en: If you describe someone as obtuse, you mean that they are slow to understand things.

words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 残忍

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: The prison conditions were inhumane.
words.ex_cn: 监狱的条件是不人道的。
words.en: If you describe something as inhumane, you mean that it is extremely cruel.

words.ex: The relentless rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 无情的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: Someone who is relentless is determined to do something and refuses to give up, even if what they are doing is unpleasant or cruel.

words.tr: adj. 严格的；缜密的；严密的；
words.ex: The teacher is rigorous about homework deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作业截止日期要求严格。
words.en: If you are rigorous in something, you are very thorough and strict in the way you do it.

words.ex: He gave a vicious smile before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前露出一个恶毒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vicious, you mean that they are violent and cruel, or that they are intended to cause someone great harm or suffering.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 有害

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.ex: Smoking is a detriment to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that causes damage, harm, or loss.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.ex: The poison is lethal to humans.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药对人类是致命的。
words.en: Something that is lethal can kill people or animals.

words.ex: The smoke from the factory is noxious.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟雾是有害的。
words.en: Something that is noxious is harmful or poisonous.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr: adj. 不利的；有害的；引起偏见的
words.ex: His actions were found to be prejudicial to the company's reputation.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为被发现对公司声誉不利。
words.en: If something is prejudicial to someone or something, it is harmful to them.

words.ex: The victim cried for help.
words.ex_cn: 受害者呼救。
words.en: A victim is someone who has been harmed, injured, or killed as a result of a crime, accident, or other event or action.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: The poison in the snake is a natural toxin.
words.ex_cn: 蛇的毒液是一种天然毒素。
words.en: A toxin is a poisonous substance, especially one produced by bacteria, which causes disease.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 懒惰

words.ex: He has a disinclination to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意在公众场合讲话。
words.en: A disinclination to do something is a feeling of not wanting to do it.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.ex: The sloth moves very slowly in the tree.
words.ex_cn: 树懒在树上移动得非常慢。
words.en: Sloth is a disinclination to work or exert oneself; laziness, or a slow-moving tropical American mammal that lives in trees.

words.ex: The turtle moves in a sluggish way.
words.ex_cn: 乌龟移动得很缓慢。
words.en: If you describe something as sluggish, you mean that it is moving or working more slowly than usual.

words.tr:
n. 一条（面包）
v. 游荡；虚度光阴
words.ex: He bought a loaf of bread from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他从面包店买了一条面包。
words.en: A loaf is a quantity of bread that is shaped and baked in one piece and usually sliced before being eaten. As a verb, to loaf means to spend time in a lazy way, doing nothing in particular.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 恶毒

words.tr: adj. 丑恶的；可怕的；丑陋的；
words.ex: The monster had a hideous face.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物有一张丑恶的脸。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is hideous, you mean that they are very ugly or unattractive.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.ex: The scandal made the news last week.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻上周上了新闻。
words.en: A scandal is a situation or event that is thought to be shocking and immoral and that everyone knows about.

words.tr: adj. 分泌毒液的；有毒的；恶毒的
words.ex: The snake is venomous.
words.ex_cn: 这条蛇是有毒的。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as venomous, you mean that they show great bitterness and anger toward someone.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 贫困

words.tr: adj. 单调乏味的；毫无变化的；
words.ex: The work is monotonous and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作单调乏味。
words.en: Something that is monotonous is very boring because it has a regular, repeated pattern which never changes.

words.ex: The needy family received food from the charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的家庭从慈善机构收到了食物。
words.en: Needy people do not have enough food, medicine, or clothing, or adequate houses.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He found himself in a predicament when he lost his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 当他丢掉钱包时，他陷入了困境。
words.en: A predicament is a difficult, perplexing, or trying situation.

words.ex: The scarcity of water caused problems in the village.
words.ex_cn: 水的缺乏给村庄带来了问题。
words.en: A scarcity of something is a situation in which there is not enough of it.

words.ex: The village has a sparse population.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄人口稀少。
words.en: Something that is sparse is small in number or amount and spread out over an area.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 傲慢

words.tr: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的
words.ex: He is complacent about his good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的好成绩感到自满。
words.en: A complacent person is very pleased with themselves or feels that they do not need to do anything about a situation, even though the situation may be uncertain or dangerous.

words.ex: He shows narcissism by always talking about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他总是谈论自己，表现出自恋。
words.en: Narcissism is the habit of always thinking about yourself and your appearance and abilities, and believing that you are better than other people.

words.ex: He wore gold chains as a show of ostentation.
words.ex_cn: 他戴金链子是为了炫耀。
words.en: Ostentation is the act of showing off your wealth, possessions, or abilities in a way that is meant to impress others.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；自负的；自以为是的
words.ex: His overweening pride led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 他过于自信的骄傲导致了他的失败。
words.en: If you describe someone as overweening, you are criticizing them because they are too confident and think they are better than other people.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；自命不凡的；浮华的
words.ex: He gave a pompous speech with big words.
words.ex_cn: 他用华丽的词藻做了一番自大的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as pompous, you mean that they behave or speak in a very serious way because they think they are more important than they really are.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.ex: He bought a new mirror because of his vanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣心买了一面新镜子。
words.en: The quality of being vain; excessive pride in or admiration of one's own appearance or achievements.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 冗长

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr: adj. 宽松的；容积大的；部头大的；卷数多的
words.ex: She wore a voluminous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条宽松的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is voluminous is very large or contains a lot of things.

chapters.name: Word List 35 负向评价 其他

words.ex: He was adamant about not changing his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他坚定不移地不改变主意。
words.en: If someone is adamant about something, they are determined not to change their mind about it.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.ex: He felt envious when his friend got a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友得到一辆新自行车时，他感到嫉妒。
words.en: If you are envious of someone, you want something that they have.

words.tr: adj. 枯萎的；无生气的；无价值的
words.ex: The tree is sapless after the winter.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在冬天后没有树液。
words.en: Lacking vitality or energy, especially as a result of being dried out or withered.

chapters.name: Word List 36 负向行为 痛苦

words.ex: The disease afflicted many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病使村子里许多人遭受痛苦。
words.en: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or misfortune, it causes you great suffering and distress.

chapters.name: Word List 36 负向行为 犯罪

words.ex: The disease afflicted many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病使村子里许多人遭受痛苦。
words.en: If you are afflicted by pain, illness, or misfortune, it causes you great suffering and distress.

words.ex: He felt guilty for lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对朋友撒谎而感到有罪。
words.en: If you feel guilty, you feel unhappy because you believe that you have done something wrong or have failed to do something which you should have done.

words.ex: The police investigated the homicide case.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了这起凶杀案。
words.en: The act of killing another person, especially when it is considered a crime.

words.ex: The police seized illicit drugs from the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警察从嫌疑人那里没收了非法毒品。
words.en: Illicit activities or substances are not allowed by law or by social or religious custom.

words.tr: v. 使负罪；指控…有罪；牵连
words.ex: He did not want to incriminate his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让他的朋友涉罪。
words.en: If something incriminates someone, it suggests that they are guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.tr: n. （医院或监狱中的）同宿者；监犯
words.ex: The inmate shared his cell with two others.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯和另外两个人共用一间牢房。
words.en: A person who is confined in a prison, hospital, or other institution.

words.tr: n. 报复；报仇；报复性劫掠
words.ex: He feared reprisal after speaking out against the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开反对老板而害怕遭到报复。
words.en: An act of retaliation for a wrong or injury.

words.ex: He tried to shoplift a shirt from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从商店偷一件衬衫。
words.en: To steal goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer.

words.ex: He tried to smuggle cigarettes across the border.
words.ex_cn: 他试图走私香烟过境。
words.en: To smuggle goods or people means to move them into or out of a country illegally.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

chapters.name: Word List 36 负向行为 掠夺

words.ex: The aliens abduct the man at night.
words.ex_cn: 外星人在晚上绑架了那个男人。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force or deception; kidnap.

words.tr:
v. 绑架；劫持；诱拐
n. 绑架罪
words.ex: The man tried to kidnap the little girl.
words.ex_cn: 这个人试图绑架那个小女孩。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force, typically to obtain a ransom.

words.tr:
adj. 被剥夺的；丧失的；失去亲人的
v. 夺去；使丧失；“bereave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was bereft of words after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他一句话也说不出来。
words.en: If someone is bereft of something, they have lost it and feel its loss keenly.

words.ex: The storm denuded the trees of their leaves.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把树上的叶子都刮掉了。
words.en: To strip something of its covering, possessions, or assets; to make bare.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.tr: v. 侵入；侵占；侵犯；侵蚀
words.ex: The new building encroaches on the park.
words.ex_cn: 新建筑侵占了公园。
words.en: To gradually take something such as power or authority from someone else, often in a way that is not fair or legal.

words.ex: The fire engulfed the old house.
words.ex_cn: 大火吞噬了那座老房子。
words.en: If one thing engulfs another, it completely covers or hides it, often in a sudden and unexpected way.

words.ex: The colors of the painting fade in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的颜色在阳光下逐渐消失。
words.en: To gradually grow faint and disappear.

words.tr: adj. 不可剥夺（或分割）的
words.ex: Freedom is an inalienable right.
words.ex_cn: 自由是不可剥夺的权利。
words.en: An inalienable right or quality is one that cannot be taken away from you.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: The new policy undercut the company's profits.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策削弱了公司的利润。
words.en: To undercut means to sell something at a lower price than a competitor, or to weaken something or someone.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

chapters.name: Word List 36 人及相关动作 视听

words.ex: The room has good acoustic properties.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有良好的声音效果。
words.en: Relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

words.ex: The bird made a soft chirp in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在早晨发出轻柔的唧唧声。
words.en: If a bird or an insect chirps, it makes short high-pitched sounds.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: The difference is discernible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异肉眼可见。
words.en: able to be discerned; perceptible

words.ex: The ghost is invisible to the human eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个鬼魂肉眼看不见。
words.en: If something is invisible, you cannot see it because it is hidden or because it is very difficult to see.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

words.ex: The children learned through visual aids like pictures.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们通过图片等视觉辅助工具学习。
words.en: relating to seeing or to the eyes

words.tr: adj. 近视的；目光短浅的
words.ex: He is short-sighted and needs glasses to see far.
words.ex_cn: 他近视，需要戴眼镜才能看远。
words.en: If someone is short-sighted, they cannot see things clearly that are far away, or they do not plan for the future in a sensible way.

words.ex: The spectator watched the game quietly.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者安静地观看了比赛。
words.en: A spectator is someone who watches an event, show, game, or activity.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

chapters.name: Word List 36 人及相关动作 身体行为

words.tr:
n. 青少年；
adj. 青少年的；
words.ex: The adolescent walked to school with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个青少年和朋友们一起走路去上学。
words.en: An adolescent is a young person who is developing into an adult.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.ex: The kidneys excrete waste from the body.
words.ex_cn: 肾脏将废物排出体外。
words.en: If someone excretes waste matter from their body, they get rid of it in faeces, urine, or sweat.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.ex: He hums a tune while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时哼着曲子。
words.en: To make a low, steady, continuous sound like that of a bee.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.ex: The soldiers raided the enemy camp at night.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在夜间突袭了敌人的营地。
words.en: A raid is a sudden attack on a place by soldiers, police, or other officials, in order to search for something or to arrest someone.

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.tr: adj. 需要久坐的；惯于久坐不动的；不爱活动的；
words.ex: His sedentary job makes him sit all day.
words.ex_cn: 他的久坐工作让他整天坐着。
words.en: Someone who has a sedentary lifestyle or job sits down a lot of the time and does not take much exercise.

words.ex: The castle endured a long siege during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争中经历了长期的围攻。
words.en: A siege is a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling those inside to surrender.

words.ex: He put a stamp on the envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他在信封上贴了一张邮票。
words.en: A stamp is a small piece of paper which you stick on an envelope or package before you post it to pay for the cost of the postage. It can also mean to bring down your foot heavily on the ground or to impress a pattern or mark on a surface.

words.ex: He changed his stance on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他改变了对气候变化的立场。
words.en: A stance is a particular way of standing, especially in sports such as golf or baseball, or a person's attitude or opinion about something, especially when it is stated publicly.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.tr:
n. 兵营；棚屋；临时工房
v. 喝倒彩；起哄
words.ex: The soldiers live in a barrack near the base.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们住在基地附近的一个兵营里。
words.en: A barrack is a building or group of buildings where soldiers live. It can also mean to provide such accommodation or to cheer someone on enthusiastically.

words.ex: His behavioral changes worried his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为变化让他的父母担心。
words.en: Relating to the way in which someone behaves.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

chapters.name: Word List 36 人及相关动作 能力

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: His inability to swim saved him from drowning.
words.ex_cn: 他不会游泳，这救了他一命。
words.en: If you refer to someone's inability to do something, you are emphasizing that they cannot do it.

chapters.name: Word List 36 人及相关动作 嗅觉

words.ex: The flowers are aromatic and fill the garden with scent.
words.ex_cn: 这些花是芳香的，使花园充满香气。
words.en: Having a pleasant and distinctive smell.

words.ex: The old house has a mysterious aura.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一种神秘的氛围。
words.en: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality that seems to surround and be generated by a person, thing, or place.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.ex: The flower has a sweet fragrance.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花有一种甜美的香味。
words.en: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, especially that of a flower or perfume.

chapters.name: Word List 36 人及相关动作 身体特征

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

words.ex: His personality is very friendly and outgoing.
words.ex_cn: 他的个性非常友好和外向。
words.en: The combination of characteristics or qualities that form an individual's distinctive character.

words.ex: The survey asks about your gender.
words.ex_cn: 这个调查询问你的性别。
words.en: Gender is the state of being male or female, especially when considered with reference to social and cultural differences, not just biological ones.

words.tr: n. 男性；男子气概；阳性
words.ex: He shows traditional masculinity by being strong and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 他通过坚强和沉默展现男性气质。
words.en: The quality or condition of being masculine; manliness.

words.tr: adj. 能吃苦耐劳的；耐寒的；
words.ex: He is a hardy farmer who works in the field all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个能吃苦耐劳的农民，整天在田里干活。
words.en: Someone who is hardy is strong and able to cope with difficult conditions.

words.ex: Honey is a viscous liquid.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是一种黏稠的液体。
words.en: A viscous liquid is thick and sticky and does not flow easily.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言&其他（一） 尖酸讽刺

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.tr:
n. 酸；
adj. 酸性的；
words.ex: The acid in lemon juice tastes sour.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬汁中的酸味道很酸。
words.en: An acid is a chemical substance, usually a liquid, which contains hydrogen and can react with other substances to form salts. Some acids burn or dissolve other substances that they come into contact with.

words.tr: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；悲观的；
words.ex: He gave a cynical smile when they talked about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 当他们谈到诚实时，他露出了愤世嫉俗的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as cynical, you mean they believe that people always act selfishly.

words.ex: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: If you say that it is ironic that something happens, you mean that it is odd or amusing because it involves a contrast or is the opposite of what you would expect.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；捅
n. 戳；刺；捅
words.ex: He poked the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke means to prod or jab someone or something with a finger or a pointed object, or to move something in a particular direction with a sharp movement. It can also refer to the act of making a hole or opening in something by pushing a pointed object into it.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言&其他（一） 批评

words.ex: They accused him of stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他们指控他偷了钱。
words.en: If you accuse someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you say or tell them that you believe that they did it.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.ex: The teacher will critique the student's essay tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会对学生的作文发表评论。
words.en: A critique is a detailed analysis and assessment of something, especially a literary, philosophical, or political theory.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.ex: He faced public denunciation for his lies.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎而遭到公众的谴责。
words.en: Denunciation is the act of criticizing something or someone strongly and publicly.

words.tr:
v. 责备；指责
n. 责备；指责
words.ex: She reproached him for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她责备他迟到了。
words.en: To express disapproval or disappointment towards someone because of their actions or behavior.

words.tr: v. 拒绝；断绝关系；否认；驳斥
words.ex: He repudiate the false claim.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这个虚假的声明。
words.en: If you repudiate something or someone, you show that you strongly disagree with them and do not want to be connected with them in any way.

words.ex: People often stigmatize those with mental illness.
words.ex_cn: 人们常常污名化患有精神疾病的人。
words.en: If someone or something is stigmatized, they are unfairly regarded by many people as being bad or having something to be ashamed of.

words.ex: He was victimized by a scammer last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被骗子欺骗了。
words.en: To victimize someone means to make them suffer as a result of your actions, especially by treating them unfairly.

words.tr: n. 中伤，诽谤（aspersion 的复数）
words.ex: He denied the aspersions about his honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了关于他诚实性的污蔑。
words.en: If someone casts aspersions on you, they suggest that you are not as good or honest as people think.

words.ex: He filed a complaint about the noisy neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他投诉了吵闹的邻居。
words.en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言&其他（一） 口才

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.ex: His eloquence moved everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的雄辩打动了房间里每一个人。
words.en: The ability to speak or write in a way that is fluent, persuasive, and expressive.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

chapters.name: Word List 37 语言&其他（一） 其他

words.ex: He stopped talking abruptly.
words.ex_cn: 他突然停止了说话。
words.en: Suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.ex: He believes in an afterlife where people meet again.
words.ex_cn: 他相信人死后会进入一个再次相聚的来世。
words.en: The afterlife is the belief that a part of, or essence of, or soul of an individual, which carries with it and may confer personal identity, survives the death of the body of this world and this lifetime, according to various worldviews.

words.tr: v. 声称；“allege”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 所谓的；
words.ex: He alleged that the witness lied.
words.ex_cn: 他声称证人说了谎。
words.en: An alleged fact has been stated but has not been proved.

words.ex: The school invited its alumni to the annual reunion.
words.ex_cn: 学校邀请了它的校友参加年度聚会。
words.en: Alumni are former students of a particular school, college, or university.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.ex: The cellular structure of plants is very small.
words.ex_cn: 植物的细胞结构非常微小。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of cells; having a porous structure.

words.ex: There is no cure-all for every illness.
words.ex_cn: 没有一种万能药能治所有病。
words.en: A cure-all is something that people think will solve all problems or cure all illnesses, often in a way that is not realistic.

words.ex: He stayed in a deluxe room at the hotel.
words.ex_cn: 他住在酒店的豪华房间里。
words.en: If you describe something as deluxe, you mean that it is very luxurious and expensive.

words.ex: He went to school despite the rain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管下雨，他还是去上学了。
words.en: Without being affected by; in spite of.

words.ex: He will encode the message with a secret code.
words.ex_cn: 他将用密钥对这条信息进行编码。
words.en: To convert information into a particular form, especially for the purposes of secrecy or transmission.

words.ex: This is an evolutionary change in the species.
words.ex_cn: 这是该物种的一种进化的改变。
words.en: Relating to or denoting processes of development or growth, especially in a biological context.

words.ex: Workers excavate the old ruins with shovels.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用铲子挖掘古代遗址。
words.en: To excavate means to dig in the ground in order to find things that have been buried there, such as archaeological remains.

words.ex: The excavation revealed ancient pottery.
words.ex_cn: 挖掘发现了古代陶器。
words.en: The process of digging up and removing earth, especially at an archaeological site.

words.ex: There are only two extant copies of the ancient book.
words.ex_cn: 这本古书现存只有两份。
words.en: If something is extant, it is still in existence, in spite of being very old.

words.ex: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was a great feat.
words.ex_cn: 在不吸氧的情况下爬山是一项伟大的壮举。
words.en: A feat is an act or achievement that shows great courage, skill, or strength.

words.tr: adj. 封建的；封建制度的
words.ex: The land was owned by feudal lords.
words.ex_cn: 土地由封建领主拥有。
words.en: Relating to, resembling, or characteristic of feudalism.

words.tr: adj. 细粒状的；颗粒状的；
words.ex: The sand feels granular between your fingers.
words.ex_cn: 沙子在你手指间感觉是细粒状的。
words.en: Granular things are composed of or resemble grains or particles.

words.ex: The hallmark of a good teacher is patience.
words.ex_cn: 好老师的标志是耐心。
words.en: A hallmark is a distinctive characteristic or attribute that is typical of a particular person or thing.

words.ex: The country seeks hegemony over its neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家试图对邻国实现霸权。
words.en: Hegemony refers to the dominance or leadership of one group or state over others, especially in a political or cultural context.

words.ex: He inherited his family's heritage.
words.ex_cn: 他继承了家族的遗产。
words.en: Heritage refers to the traditions, achievements, beliefs, etc., that are part of the history of a group or nation.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.tr:
v. 突出；强调；高光；
n. 最突出的部分；
words.ex: The teacher highlighted the key words in the text.
words.ex_cn: 老师把文中的关键词突出了。
words.en: To highlight something means to make it stand out or to emphasize it, often because it is important or interesting.

words.tr: adj. 冰磨的；冰川磨光的
words.ex: The rocks in the valley were ice-polished, indicating the presence of ancient glaciers.
words.ex_cn: 山谷中的岩石经过冰磨，表明这里曾有古冰川存在。
words.en: Having been made smooth and shiny by the action of ice.

words.ex: He idealizes his father as a perfect hero.
words.ex_cn: 他把父亲理想化为一个完美的英雄。
words.en: To regard or represent as perfect or more nearly perfect than is true.

words.tr: n. 即时性；直接性；迫切性
words.ex: The immediacy of the response surprised her.
words.ex_cn: 回复的即时性让她感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being immediate or happening without delay.

words.ex: The accident immobilized his leg.
words.ex_cn: 事故使他的腿无法动弹。
words.en: To prevent something or someone from moving or operating as normal.

words.tr: v. 即兴创作；即兴表演；临时准备；
words.ex: He improvise a song on the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他即兴创作了一首钢琴曲。
words.en: If you improvise, you make or do something using whatever you have or without having planned it in advance.

words.tr: adj. 不完全的；不完整的；
words.ex: The puzzle is incomplete without the last piece.
words.ex_cn: 没有最后一块，这个拼图是不完全的。
words.en: If something is incomplete, it is not yet finished, or it does not have all the parts that it should have.

words.tr: adj. 无结论的；非决定性的；不确定的
words.ex: The test results were inconclusive.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果没有定论。
words.en: If research or evidence is inconclusive, it has not proved anything.

words.tr: adj. 在职的；负有义务的；
words.ex: The incumbent mayor won the election again.
words.ex_cn: 现任市长再次赢得了选举。
words.en: An incumbent is someone who currently holds a particular office or position, especially in politics. It can also refer to something that is necessary as a duty or responsibility.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.tr: adj. 水生的；水栖的；水中的；
words.ex: The fish live in aquatic plants.
words.ex_cn: 这些鱼生活在水生植物中。
words.en: Relating to water; living in or near water or taking place in water.

words.tr: vt. 铭记于心；使不朽；防腐；使充满香气
words.ex: They embalm the memory of their hero.
words.ex_cn: 他们铭记着英雄的记忆。
words.en: To embalm a dead body means to treat it with special substances to prevent it from decaying.

words.ex: The new app is an offshoot of the original website.
words.ex_cn: 这个新应用是原网站的衍生物。
words.en: An offshoot is something that has developed from something larger or more general.

words.tr:
adj. 特指的；特殊的；挑剔的；
n. 细节；详情；
words.ex: He wants a particular book, not any other.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一本特指的书，不是别的。
words.en: You use particular to emphasize that you are talking about one thing or one kind of thing rather than other similar ones.

words.tr:
n. 谓语；述语
v. 使基于；断言；宣布
words.ex: He uses a simple predicate to explain the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的谓语来解释这个句子。
words.en: If you predicate something, you base it on or say that it depends on something else. In grammar, the predicate of a clause is the part of it that is not the subject.

words.tr:
v. 注册；登记；
n. 登记簿；
words.ex: He will register for the course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会注册这门课程。
words.en: If you register something, you officially record it or list it.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.tr:
n. 替罪羊；代人受过者
v. 使…成为替罪羊
words.ex: He was made the scapegoat for the company's financial failures.
words.ex_cn: 他被当作公司财务失败的替罪羊。
words.en: A scapegoat is a person who is blamed for something that someone else has done.

words.ex: He got the promotion because of his seniority.
words.ex_cn: 他因为资历深而获得了晋升。
words.en: Seniority is the state of being older or higher in rank than someone else.

words.ex: This factory specializes in making electric cars.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂专用于制造电动汽车。
words.en: If you specialize in a particular subject or skill, you become an expert in it by focusing your studies or work on it.

words.tr:
n. 针脚；缝线；一针
v. 缝；缝合
words.ex: She sews a stitch to fix the tear.
words.ex_cn: 她缝一针来补破洞。
words.en: A stitch is a piece of thread that has been used to sew the edges of a wound together. It can also refer to a loop of thread or yarn resulting from a single pass or movement of the needle in sewing, knitting, or crocheting.

words.ex: The teacher has a long tenure at the school.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师在学校有很长的任期。
words.en: The period during which an office is held; the status of holding one's position on a permanent basis.

words.tr:
v. （使）发痒；胳肢；逗乐
n. 痒；胳肢；呵痒
words.ex: The feather tickles my arm.
words.ex_cn: 羽毛挠得我手臂发痒。
words.en: If something tickles you, it touches you in a way that makes you laugh or feel slightly uncomfortable, usually because it is touching a sensitive part of your body. If something tickles you, it also makes you feel amused or pleased.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: The forest is a virgin land, untouched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是未开发的土地，从未被人类触及过。
words.en: A virgin is someone who has never had sexual intercourse. It can also describe something that is in its original pure or natural condition and has not been touched or changed by people.

words.ex: He is virtually always on time.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎总是准时。
words.en: In effect though not formally recognized; practically.

words.ex: The eagle has a wide wingspan.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹰的翼展很宽。
words.en: The wingspan of a bird or an aircraft is the distance from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other wing.

words.tr: n. 活力；生命力；精力；子弹声; vt. 对……挑剔; vi. 发尖啸声
words.ex: She brought a new zing to the company with her innovative ideas.
words.ex_cn: 她用她的创新想法给公司带来了新的活力。
words.en: If you say that something has zing, you mean that it is full of energy, excitement, or interest.

chapters.name: Word List 38 其他（二） 首尾

words.ex: He showed his entree to the concert hall.
words.ex_cn: 他向音乐厅出示了他的入场许可。
words.en: The main course of a meal; the act of entering.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.ex: He read the preface before starting the book.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始读这本书之前读了序言。
words.en: A preface is an introduction at the beginning of a book, which explains what the book is about or why it was written.

words.ex: He acted as an intermediary between the two sides.
words.ex_cn: 他充当了双方之间的中间人。
words.en: An intermediary is a person who acts as a link between people or groups in order to try to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: He is an intermediate student in English.
words.ex_cn: 他是英语的中级学生。
words.en: An intermediate stage, level, or position is one that occurs between two other stages, levels, or positions.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.tr: adj. 无可置疑的；决定性的；
words.ex: The evidence was conclusive.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可置疑的。
words.en: If something is conclusive, it means that it proves something in a way that is certain and leaves no doubt.

words.ex: The demise of the old king shocked the nation.
words.ex_cn: 老国王的去世震惊了全国。
words.en: The demise of something or someone is their end or death.

words.ex: The denouement of the story was surprising.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的结局令人惊讶。
words.en: The final part of a play, movie, or narrative in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and matters are explained or resolved.

words.ex: The train's destination is Beijing.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车的目的地是北京。
words.en: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

words.tr: n. 分支；支流；衍生物；后果
words.ex: The ramification of the tree spread wide.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树的分支延伸得很广。
words.en: A ramification is a complex or unwelcome consequence of an action or decision.

words.tr: n. 弹回；反响；后果；反射
words.ex: The ball showed a clear repercussion off the wall.
words.ex_cn: 球从墙上明显地弹回。
words.en: The effect that an action, event, or decision has on something, especially a bad effect.

words.ex: The water in the pond was stagnant.
words.ex_cn: 池塘里的水不流动。
words.en: If something such as a business or economy is stagnant, there is little activity or change.

words.tr: v. （使）停滞；不发展；因不流动而变得污浊
words.ex: The economy began to stagnate after the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 经济在危机后开始停滞。
words.en: If something such as a business or project stagnates, it stops developing or making progress.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.ex: The movie had a sequel that came out last year.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一部去年上映的续集。
words.en: A sequel is a book, film, or play that continues the story of a previous one.

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

chapters.name: Word List 38 其他（二） 物质

words.tr:
n. 鹅卵石
v. 修补（鞋）；粗制滥造
words.ex: He cobbled together a shoe from old leather.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧皮革拼凑了一双鞋。
words.en: To cobble means to make or assemble something in a rough or improvised way, or to pave with cobblestones.

words.ex: She wore a ring with an emerald.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一枚镶有翡翠的戒指。
words.en: An emerald is a precious stone which is clear and bright green.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.tr: adj. 非物质的；无形的；不重要的
words.ex: The color is immaterial to the function.
words.ex_cn: 颜色对功能无关紧要。
words.en: If you say that something is immaterial, you mean that it is not important or not relevant.

words.tr: n. 纪念品；用以回忆的东西
words.ex: She keeps a photo as a memento of her trip.
words.ex_cn: 她保留了一张照片作为旅行的纪念品。
words.en: A memento is an object which you keep because it reminds you of a person or a special event.

words.ex: The completion of the project was a significant milepost in our company's history.
words.ex_cn: 项目的完成是我们公司历史上的一个重要里程碑。
words.en: A milepost is a sign or marker placed at the side of a road to indicate the distance in miles to a particular place.

words.ex: The floor has a colorful mosaic of flowers.
words.ex_cn: 地板上有一个五彩的花卉镶嵌图案。
words.en: A mosaic is a picture or pattern produced by arranging together small colored pieces of hard material, such as stone, tile, or glass.

words.ex: A mote of dust floated in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 一粒微尘在阳光中飘浮。
words.en: A very small piece of a substance, especially dust.

words.tr:
n. V字形刻痕；等级；切口
v. 赢得；刻凹痕
words.ex: He made a notch on the stick to count days.
words.ex_cn: 他在木棍上刻了一个刻痕来计数天数。
words.en: A notch is a small cut or indentation in a surface. It can also refer to a level or degree in a scale or a narrow pass between mountains.

words.tr:
n. 假发
v. 痛骂；严责；给…装假发
words.ex: She wore a wig to cover her bald head.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一顶假发来遮盖她光秃的头。
words.en: A wig is a covering of false hair which you wear on your head, for example because you are bald or because you want to cover up your own hair.

chapters.name: Word List 38 其他（二） 逻辑

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: He generalized the results from the small group to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他将小群体的结果概括为全体情况。
words.en: If you generalize, you say something that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: From the clues, he made a logical inference.
words.ex_cn: 从线索中，他做出了一个合理的推论。
words.en: An inference is a conclusion that you draw about something by using information that you already have about it.

words.ex: He is methodical in organizing his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在安排工作时很有条理。
words.en: If you describe someone as methodical, you mean that they do things carefully, thoroughly, and in order.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: It is rational to save money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 为未来存钱是合理的。
words.en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.

words.tr: n. 基本原理；基础理论；
words.ex: The rationale for the new rule is to save time.
words.ex_cn: 这个新规则的基本原理是节省时间。
words.en: The fundamental reasons or logical basis for a course of action or belief.

words.tr: adj. 不合理的；没有根据的；无端的
words.ex: The teacher gave an unwarranted warning.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个没有理由的警告。
words.en: If you describe something as unwarranted, you are critical of it because there is no need or reason for it.

chapters.name: Word List 38 其他（二） 主义

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

chapters.name: Word List 39 词组

words.ex: His altruism made him donate all his money to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的利他主义让他把所有钱捐给了穷人。
words.en: Altruism is the belief in or practice of disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

words.tr: phrase. 考虑到；体谅；允许有；留出
words.ex: The plan allows for extra time if needed.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划为需要时留出了额外的时间。
words.en: To make provision or plans for something; to take into consideration.

words.ex: Workers stand on the assembly line to put parts together.
words.ex_cn: 工人们站在装配线上组装零件。
words.en: An assembly line is a manufacturing process in which parts are added to a product in a sequential manner to create a finished product.

words.ex: He solved the problem at one stroke.
words.ex_cn: 他一下子就解决了问题。
words.en: If something happens at one stroke, it happens suddenly and completely, often as the result of a single action.

words.tr: phrase. 在危险中；处于成败关头
words.ex: His job is at stake if he is late again.
words.ex_cn: 如果他再迟到，他的工作就保不住了。
words.en: If something is at stake, it is being risked and might be lost or damaged if something goes wrong.

words.tr: 短语. 有争议的；成为争论焦点的
words.ex: What he said is at issue.
words.ex_cn: 他说的话是争议的焦点。
words.en: To be the subject of debate or dispute.

words.tr: phrase. 定价过高使…无力购买；因价格过高而被排除在外
words.ex: The new phone prices out of reach for most students.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机的价格让大多数学生买不起。
words.en: To make something too expensive for someone to afford by setting a high price.

words.tr: phrase. 状况好转的；经济状况好的
words.ex: He is better off staying home instead of going out in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他待在家里比在雨天外出更好。
words.en: If you are better off, you are in a better situation, usually because you have more money.

words.ex: Hard work can bring about success.
words.ex_cn: 努力工作可以带来成功。
words.en: To cause something to happen.

words.tr: phrase. 呼吁；号召；要求；接（人）
words.ex: The situation calls for immediate action.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况需要立即采取行动。
words.en: If you call for something, you demand that it should happen.

words.tr: phrase. 以…为中心；重点在于…
words.ex: The lesson centers on basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这节课的重点是基本数学技能。
words.en: To have something as the main subject of attention or interest.

words.ex: He still clings to his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他仍然坚持自己的旧信念。
words.en: To hold on tightly to something or someone, either physically or emotionally, often because of fear, love, or a strong desire.

words.tr: phrase. 夏令时；日光节约时间（指在夏季将时钟调快一小时以充分利用日光）
words.ex: Daylight saving time is observed in many countries to maximize daylight hours.
words.ex_cn: 许多国家实行夏令时以最大化日光时间。
words.en: Daylight saving time is the period during which the time is adjusted forward by one hour from the standard time, usually to make better use of daylight in the evenings.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 深入探究；深入研究
words.ex: He delves into ancient history books.
words.ex_cn: 他深入钻研古代历史书籍。
words.en: To delve into something means to try to discover new information about it or to examine it in detail.

words.tr: phrase. 损害；减损；降低……的价值或重要性
words.ex: Don't let small mistakes detract from your great progress.
words.ex_cn: 不要让小错误削弱你的巨大进步。
words.en: To reduce the value, importance, or quality of something.

words.ex: Many old traditions die out over time.
words.ex_cn: 许多古老的传统随着时间推移而消失。
words.en: If something dies out, it becomes less and less common and eventually disappears completely.

words.tr: phrase. 过分喜爱；溺爱；对……非常疼爱
words.ex: She likes to dote on her grandchildren.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢溺爱她的孙子孙女。
words.en: To show excessive love or fondness for someone, often to the point of spoiling them.

words.tr: phrase. 陷入常规；变得单调乏味；进入一成不变的状态
words.ex: He felt his daily routine fall into a rut.
words.ex_cn: 他感觉自己的日常生活陷入了一成不变的境地。
words.en: To become stuck in a monotonous or unvarying routine or pattern of behavior.

words.tr: phrase. 实地研究；现场调查；田野调查
words.ex: The anthropologist conducted a field study to understand local customs.
words.ex_cn: 人类学家进行了实地研究，以了解当地的习俗。
words.en: A field study is a research method that involves observing and interacting with subjects in their natural environment to collect data.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 闲荡；胡闹；不认真对待
words.ex: The boys are fooling around in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 那些男孩在教室里瞎闹。
words.en: To spend time doing things that are not useful or serious.

words.tr: phrase. 使适合于，调整以适应（某事物）；使针对
words.ex: The school gears its lessons to the students' needs.
words.ex_cn: 学校将课程调整为适应学生的需求。
words.en: To adjust or adapt something to suit a particular purpose, need, or audience.

words.tr: phrase. v. 度过难关；勉强应付；勉强维持生活
words.ex: He gets by with little money.
words.ex_cn: 他靠很少的钱维持生活。
words.en: To manage to live or do a particular thing using the money, knowledge, equipment, etc. that you have.

words.tr: phrase. 通过；（电话）打通；度过；做完；用完
words.ex: He got through the exam with help from his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在朋友的帮助下通过了考试。
words.en: To succeed in reaching a place or a stage in a process, or to make someone understand or accept something.

words.ex: Poor hygiene can give rise to infections.
words.ex_cn: 不良的卫生习惯可能导致感染。
words.en: To cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: The old rules give way to new ones.
words.ex_cn: 旧规则让位于新规则。
words.en: If something gives way to something else, it is replaced by it.

words.tr: phrase. 政府干预；指政府为影响经济或社会活动而采取的措施或行动
words.ex: The government intervention helped stabilize the economy.
words.ex_cn: 政府干预帮助稳定了经济。
words.en: Government intervention refers to the actions taken by a government to affect the economy or society, often to correct market failures or to achieve a social or economic objective.

words.tr: phrase. 热门节目；受欢迎的演出
words.ex: The new drama became a hit show overnight.
words.ex_cn: 这部新剧一夜之间成为了热门节目。
words.en: A hit show refers to a television program or theatrical performance that has achieved great popularity and success.

words.tr: phrase. 盛开；处于全盛时期；繁花似锦
words.ex: The garden is in full bloom in spring.
words.ex_cn: phrase. 春天，花园里的花都盛开了。
words.en: If a plant or tree is in full bloom, it has all its flowers fully open.

words.tr: phrase. 以实物（而非金钱）；以同样方式；回以同类事物
words.ex: She repaid his help in kind by offering her assistance when he needed it.
words.ex_cn: 她以同样的方式回报了他的帮助，在他需要时提供了帮助。
words.en: If you do something in kind, you do the same thing to someone that they have just done to you.

words.tr: phrase. 在某种程度上，就某种程度而言
words.ex: He will help you insofar as he can.
words.ex_cn: 他能帮多少就帮多少。
words.en: to the extent or degree that

words.ex: The company will lay off 50 workers next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将裁员50人。
words.en: To terminate the employment of a worker or workers, especially temporarily, because there is not enough work for them to do.

words.tr: phrase. 现场演出；现场表演；直播节目
words.ex: The band gave an electrifying live show last night.
words.ex_cn: 昨晚乐队进行了一场令人振奋的现场表演。
words.en: A live show is a performance, such as a concert or play, that is performed in front of an audience and broadcasted in real-time.

words.ex: You must look to your health before it's too late.
words.ex_cn: 你必须注意你的健康，趁还来得及。
words.en: To expect or depend on someone or something to do something or provide something.

words.tr: phrase. 使收支相抵；勉强维持生计；量入为出
words.ex: He works two jobs to make ends meet.
words.ex_cn: 他做两份工作来维持生计。
words.en: To have enough money to pay for the things that you need.

words.tr: phrase. 使收支相抵；勉强维持生计；量入为出
words.ex: He works two jobs to make both ends meet.
words.ex_cn: 他做两份工作来维持收支平衡。
words.en: To have enough money to pay for the things that you need.

words.ex: More often than not, he walks to school.
words.ex_cn: 大多数情况下，他走路去上学。
words.en: If you say that something happens more often than not, you mean that it happens more than half the time.

words.tr: phrase. 比以往任何时候都更；更加；愈发
words.ex: He is working harder more than ever before.
words.ex_cn: 他比以往任何时候都更加努力工作。
words.en: To a greater extent or degree than ever before.

words.tr: 短语. 意见不一致的；处于冲突状态的；互相矛盾的
words.ex: The two parties have been at odds over the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党在新政策上一直存在分歧。
words.en: If someone is at odds with someone else, or if two people are at odds, they disagree about something.

words.tr: phrase. 违者处死；以死刑相威胁；违令者格杀勿论
words.ex: You are forbidden to enter this area on pain of death.
words.ex_cn: 你被禁止进入这个区域，否则将以死相逼。
words.en: Under the threat of being killed.

words.tr: phrase. 除了…以外；不包括；绝不是
words.ex: He eats vegetables other than potatoes.
words.ex_cn: 他吃蔬菜，但不吃土豆。
words.en: You use 'other than' after a negative statement to say that the person, item, or thing that follows is the only exception to the statement.

words.tr: phrase. 黄金时段收视率；指电视台在晚间最受欢迎时段所获得的观众数量指标
words.ex: The show achieved high prime-time ratings.
words.ex_cn: 该节目获得了很高的黄金时段收视率。
words.en: The viewership statistics for television programs broadcast during the most popular and competitive evening hours.

words.ex: He left home prior to sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 他在日出前离开了家。
words.en: Before a particular time or event.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.tr: phrase. 驶离；离开；脱身；拉开距离
words.ex: The car started to pull away from the bus stop.
words.ex_cn: 汽车开始从公交站开走了。
words.en: To move away or depart, especially in a vehicle; to create distance between oneself and someone or something.

words.ex: He had to resort to asking for help.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不求助于别人。
words.en: If you resort to a particular course of action, you do it because other methods have failed.

words.tr: phrase. 经验法则；粗略估计；拇指规则（指基于经验的粗略判断而非精确计算）
words.ex: He uses the rule of thumb to estimate the cost.
words.ex_cn: 他用经验法则来估算成本。
words.en: A rule of thumb is a principle with broad application that is not intended to be strictly accurate or reliable for every situation.

words.ex: He shut off the lights before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前关掉了灯。
words.en: To stop the operation or flow of something by turning a switch, valve, or other control.

words.ex: The medicine has a side effect of dizziness.
words.ex_cn: 这种药有头晕的副作用。
words.en: An effect of a drug or chemical that is in addition to its intended effect, especially an effect that is harmful or unpleasant.

words.tr: phrase. 大声说；毫无顾虑地说出
words.ex: She decided to speak out about the unfair rule.
words.ex_cn: 她决定大声说出这个不公平的规定。
words.en: To express one's opinions openly and without fear, especially in a situation where it might be difficult or dangerous to do so.

words.tr: phrase. 表示异议；提出反对；争论
words.ex: I have to take issue with your statement that all politicians are corrupt.
words.ex_cn: 我不得不对你的说法——所有政客都是腐败的——提出异议。
words.en: To disagree with or challenge a statement or opinion.

words.ex: Safety takes precedence over speed.
words.ex_cn: 安全比速度更重要。
words.en: To be more important than something else and to be dealt with first.

words.tr: phrase. 白令海（位于太平洋北部，介于阿拉斯加与西伯利亚之间）
words.ex: The Bering Sea is known for its rich marine life.
words.ex_cn: 白令海以其丰富的海洋生物而闻名。
words.en: A marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean, located between Alaska and Russia, known for its rich marine life and harsh weather conditions.

words.tr: phrase. 美国联邦储备系统（美国的中央银行体系）
words.ex: The Federal Reserve plays a crucial role in the U.S. economy by setting monetary policy.
words.ex_cn: 联邦储备系统通过制定货币政策在美国经济中扮演着关键角色。
words.en: The Federal Reserve, often referred to as the Fed, is the central banking system of the United States, which regulates the U.S. monetary and financial system.

words.ex: The Great Lakes are a series of interconnected freshwater lakes located primarily in the upper mid-east region of North America.
words.ex_cn: 五大湖是一系列主要位于北美中东部地区的相互连接的淡水湖。
words.en: The Great Lakes are a group of five large freshwater lakes in North America, consisting of Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, Lake Erie, and Lake Ontario. They are located on or near the Canada–United States border.

words.tr: phrase. 华沙条约组织；华沙公约（指1955年由苏联及其东欧盟国签订的军事同盟条约）
words.ex: The Warsaw Pact was a military alliance of communist states in Central and Eastern Europe.
words.ex_cn: 华沙条约组织是中欧和东欧共产主义国家的一个军事联盟。
words.en: The Warsaw Pact was a collective defense treaty among the Soviet Union and seven other Soviet satellite states in Central and Eastern Europe during the Cold War.

words.tr: phrase. 权衡；交换；在……之间做出取舍
words.ex: You need to trade off cost against quality when making your decision.
words.ex_cn: 在做决定时，你需要在成本和质量之间进行权衡。
words.en: A trade-off is a situation where you must choose between or balance two things that are opposite or cannot be had at the same time.

words.tr: phrase. 以……折价换购……；用……换取……
words.ex: He traded his old bike in for a new one.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧自行车换成了新的。
words.en: To exchange something, typically an older item, for a newer or different one, often with an additional payment.

words.ex: Please turn down the volume, it's too loud.
words.ex_cn: 请把音量调低，太大声了。
words.en: To refuse or reject an offer or request; to reduce the volume, temperature, or intensity of something.

words.tr: phrase. 诚意；诚实；真实意图（拉丁语，常用于法律语境中）
words.ex: The document was submitted as evidence of his bona fides.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件被提交作为他真诚意愿的证据。
words.en: The quality of being genuine or real; sincerity and honesty.

chapters.name: Word List 40 MBA 词汇

words.tr: phrase. 商业模式；经营模式
words.ex: The company changed its business model to sell online.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司改变了商业模式，改为在线销售。
words.en: A business model describes the rationale of how an organization creates, delivers, and captures value.

words.tr: phrase. 核心竞争力；组织或个人最关键的技能或能力，使其在竞争中具有优势
words.ex: Problem solving is a core competency for every engineer.
words.ex_cn: 解决问题是每位工程师的核心能力。
words.en: The principal strength or most important ability of a company or organization.

words.tr: phrase. 竞争优势；企业或个人在市场竞争中相对于竞争对手所具备的有利条件或优势
words.ex: This company has a competitive advantage because its products are cheaper.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司因为产品更便宜而具有竞争优势。
words.en: A condition or circumstance that puts a company in a favorable or superior business position.

words.tr: phrase. 强弱危机分析；四点分析(SWOT = Strength, Weakness, Opportunity, Threats)
words.ex: The company conducted a SWOT analysis to identify its strengths and weaknesses.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了优势、劣势、机会和威胁分析，以确定其强项和弱项。
words.en: A SWOT analysis is a strategic planning method used to evaluate the Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats involved in a project or in a business venture.

words.tr: phrase. 摇钱树；赚钱利器；能持续带来稳定收入的产品或业务
words.ex: This franchise has become a cash cow for the company.
words.ex_cn: 这个特许经营权已经成为公司的摇钱树。
words.en: A cash cow is a product, service, or business that generates a steady, significant income or profit with little effort or investment.

words.ex: This segment of the book is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的这一部分非常有趣。
words.en: A segment of something is one of the parts into which it is divided or from which it is formed.

words.ex: The health sector needs more funding.
words.ex_cn: 医疗部门需要更多资金。
words.en: A particular area of activity, especially one that is part of a larger area of activity or one that is considered separately from other areas.

words.ex: The company made a subdivision of its market by age.
words.ex_cn: 公司按年龄对市场进行了细分。
words.en: A subdivision is a part or section of something which is itself divided into parts.

words.ex: The marketing mix is crucial for determining the success of a product launch.
words.ex_cn: 营销组合对于产品发布的成功至关重要。
words.en: The combination of factors that can be controlled by a company to influence consumers to purchase its products.

words.tr: phrase. 直接营销；一种不通过中间商，直接向消费者推销产品或服务的营销方式
words.ex: Direct marketing campaigns often involve personalized messages to target specific demographics.
words.ex_cn: 直接营销活动通常涉及针对特定人群的个性化信息。
words.en: Direct marketing is a form of advertising which allows businesses to communicate straight to the customer, with advertising techniques such as fliers, online display ads, emails, and promotional letters.

words.tr: phrase. 耶稣受难日（复活节前的星期五）
words.ex: They attended a church service on Good Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他们在耶稣受难日参加了一个教堂礼拜。
words.en: Good Friday is a Christian holiday commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his death at Calvary.

words.tr: phrase. 复活节星期日，基督教纪念耶稣复活的节日，通常在每年春分月圆后的第一个星期日
words.ex: Easter Sunday is a significant Christian holiday celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
words.ex_cn: 复活节星期日是基督教庆祝耶稣基督复活的重大节日。
words.en: The Sunday on which the festival of Easter is celebrated.

words.ex: The Ascension of Jesus is a significant event in Christian theology.
words.ex_cn: 耶稣升天是基督教神学中的一个重要事件。
words.en: The act of rising or moving upward; the act of ascending.

words.tr: phrase. 公司财务；企业融资
words.ex: She decided to specialize in corporate finance after graduating.
words.ex_cn: 她毕业后决定专攻公司财务。
words.en: Corporate finance is the area of finance dealing with the sources of funding and the capital structure of corporations, the actions that managers take to increase the value of the firm to the shareholders, and the tools and analysis used to allocate financial resources.

words.tr: phrase. 金融经济学；研究金融市场、资产定价、投资决策等经济行为的学科
words.ex: Financial economics focuses on the allocation and deployment of economic resources, both spatially and across time, in an uncertain environment.
words.ex_cn: 金融经济学关注的是在不确定的环境中，经济资源在空间和时间上的分配和部署。
words.en: Financial economics is a branch of economics that analyzes the use and distribution of resources in markets in which decisions are made under uncertainty.

words.tr: n. 资产流动性；资产变现能力
words.ex: The company is facing a liquidity crisis due to the sudden drop in sales.
words.ex_cn: 由于销售额的突然下降，该公司正面临流动性危机。
words.en: Liquidity refers to the availability of liquid assets to a market or company. Liquid assets are those that can be quickly converted into cash without significantly affecting their value.

words.tr: phrase. 风险投资；创业资本
words.ex: The startup secured a substantial amount of venture capital.
words.ex_cn: 这家初创公司获得了大量风险投资。
words.en: Venture capital is capital that is invested in projects that have a high risk of failure, but also a potential for high returns.

words.ex: The exit is near the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 出口在楼梯附近。
words.en: To exit means to go out of or leave a place.

words.ex: The company's Initial Public Offering was a huge success.
words.ex_cn: 该公司的首次公开发行取得了巨大成功。
words.en: An initial public offering (IPO) refers to the process of offering shares of a private corporation to the public in a new stock issuance.

words.tr: abbr. 首次公开募股；“Initial Public Offerings”的缩写
words.ex: The company plans to go public with an IPO next year.
words.ex_cn: 该公司计划明年通过首次公开募股上市。
words.en: An IPO, or Initial Public Offering, is the process by which a private company can go public by sale of its stocks to the general public.

words.tr:
n. 收获；收成；
v. 收获；收割；
words.ex: The farmers celebrated the harvest in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 农民们在秋天庆祝收获。
words.en: The harvest is the process of gathering mature crops from the fields. It is a crucial activity in agriculture that marks the end of the growing season.

words.ex: The institutional investor bought shares in the company.
words.ex_cn: 这家机构投资者购买了该公司的股票。
words.en: An institutional investor is a company or organization that invests money on behalf of other people. Examples include insurance companies, pension funds, and mutual funds.

words.ex: The store offers multiple flavors of ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供多种口味的冰淇淋。
words.en: If something is multiple, it consists of or involves many things of the same kind.

words.tr: phrase. 投资组合公司；被私募股权或风险投资公司所持有的公司
words.ex: The investor owns a portfolio company that makes shoes.
words.ex_cn: 这位投资者拥有一家生产鞋子的被投资公司。
words.en: A portfolio company is a company or entity in which a venture capital firm, private equity firm, or other investment entity has invested.

words.ex: The upside of working late is more money.
words.ex_cn: 加班的好处是能赚更多钱。
words.en: The upside is the more positive aspect of a situation that is generally bad.

words.tr: n. 获得；得到的东西；收购；
words.ex: The acquisition of new skills takes time.
words.ex_cn: 获得新技能需要时间。
words.en: An acquisition is something that someone buys, often to add to a collection of things.

words.tr: phrase. 咨询委员会；顾问董事会
words.ex: The advisory board gives advice to the school.
words.ex_cn: 顾问委员会向学校提供建议。
words.en: An advisory board is a group of people whose role is to give advice and support to an organization or project.

words.ex: This test is a benchmark for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试是所有学生的标准。
words.en: A benchmark is something whose quality or quantity is known and which can therefore be used as a standard with which other things can be compared.

words.tr: phrase. 燃烧速率；资金消耗率（尤指初创公司在盈利前每月消耗的现金量）
words.ex: The startup's burn rate is too high.
words.ex_cn: 这家初创公司的资金消耗速度太快了。
words.en: The speed at which a company spends money, especially venture capital, before it becomes profitable.

words.tr: phrase. 债务融资；通过借款或发行债券等方式筹集资金
words.ex: The company uses debt financing to buy new machines.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司通过债务融资来购买新机器。
words.en: Debt financing refers to the process of raising capital by borrowing money, typically through loans or the issuance of bonds.

words.tr: phrase. 尽职调查；应有的勤勉，尤指在商业交易前对相关事项进行的全面审查
words.ex: The company did due diligence before buying the land.
words.ex_cn: 公司在购买土地前进行了尽职调查。
words.en: The process of examining the details of a situation or the financial records of a company, especially in order to make sure that it is safe to invest in it or to do business with it.

words.tr: phrase. 股权融资；通过出售公司股份来筹集资金的方式
words.ex: The startup used equity financing to grow its business.
words.ex_cn: 这家初创公司通过股权融资来发展业务。
words.en: Equity financing is a method of raising capital through the sale of shares in an enterprise.

words.tr: phrase. 持有期；持有时间（指持有资产或投资的时间长度）
words.ex: He kept the stock for a holding period of two years.
words.ex_cn: 他持有这只股票两年的持有期。
words.en: The length of time an investment is held by an investor.

words.tr: n. 孵卵器；育婴箱；培养的器具
words.ex: The eggs are kept in an incubator to hatch.
words.ex_cn: 鸡蛋放在孵卵器里孵化。
words.en: An incubator is a piece of hospital equipment which helps weak or small babies to survive. It consists of a transparent container in which the oxygen supply, temperature, and humidity can be controlled.

words.tr: phrase. 内部收益率；使投资项目净现值为零的贴现率
words.ex: The company calculated the internal rate of return to decide if the project is worth investing in.
words.ex_cn: 公司计算了内部收益率，以决定是否值得投资这个项目。
words.en: The internal rate of return is a metric used in financial analysis to estimate the profitability of potential investments. It is the discount rate that makes the net present value of all cash flows from a particular project equal to zero.

words.tr: abbr. 内部收益率（Internal Rate of Return）；伊朗里亚尔（伊朗货币符号，...
words.ex: He gave an irr response to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个不合理的回答。
words.en: Internal Rate of Return; a financial metric used to estimate the profitability of potential investments, representing the discount rate that makes the net present value of cash flows zero.

words.tr: phrase. 杠杆收购；借债收购
words.ex: The company used a leveraged buy-out to take over its rival.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司通过杠杆收购收购了它的竞争对手。
words.en: A leveraged buy-out (LBO) is the acquisition of another company using a significant amount of borrowed money (bonds or loans) to meet the cost of acquisition. The assets of the company being acquired are often used as collateral for the loans, along with the assets of the acquiring company.

words.ex: The company was bought through an lbo.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司通过杠杆收购被买下。
words.en: A leveraged buyout (LBO) is the acquisition of another company using a significant amount of borrowed money (bonds or loans) to meet the cost of acquisition.

words.tr: phrase. 管理层收购；外部管理团队通过购入股权接管公司
words.ex: The team needs management buy-in to start the new project.
words.ex_cn: 团队需要管理层的支持才能启动新项目。
words.en: A management buy-in (MBI) occurs when an external management team buys a company and replaces the existing management team.

words.tr: n. 管理基本指标（Management by Indicators）
words.ex: The company mbi is launching a new product next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司MBI下个月将推出一款新产品。
words.en: Mean Bias Indicator; a statistical measure used to assess the average deviation of a dataset from a reference point or target value.

words.tr: phrase. 管理收购；治理收购；企业管理人员收购股权
words.ex: The employees did a management buy-out to own the company.
words.ex_cn: 员工们通过管理层收购来拥有这家公司。
words.en: A management buyout (MBO) is a form of acquisition where a company's existing managers acquire a large part or all of the company from the existing owners.

words.tr: abbr. 管理层收购；“management buyout”的缩写
words.ex: The word 'mbo' is not a standard English word.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'mbo' 不是标准的英语单词。
words.en: Mean Bias Offset; a term used in statistics or engineering to describe the systematic error or average difference between measured values and true values.

words.tr: phrase. 私募股权；私人股本；私募股权投资（指通过非公开市场投资于非上市公司股权的资本）
words.ex: He works in private equity and helps buy companies.
words.ex_cn: 他从事私募股权工作，帮助收购公司。
words.en: Private equity is a type of investment that involves investing in companies that are not publicly traded on a stock exchange.

words.tr: phrase. 条款清单；投资意向书（通常用于风险投资或并购交易中，列明交易的主要条款和条件）
words.ex: The investor gave him a term sheet for the deal.
words.ex_cn: 投资者给了他一份交易条款清单。
words.en: A term sheet is a non-binding agreement setting forth the basic terms and conditions under which an investment will be made.

words.ex: The company's turnaround came after new management took over.
words.ex_cn: 公司在新管理层接手后发生了转变。
words.en: A turnaround is a complete change in a situation or in the way that someone behaves.

words.ex: His entrepreneurship helped start a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他的企业家精神帮助创办了一家小企业。
words.en: Entrepreneurship is the activity of setting up a business or businesses, taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.

words.tr: phrase. 人力资源管理，指组织中负责招聘、培训、绩效评估、薪酬福利和员工关系等与人员相关的管理活动
words.ex: He works in human resources management at a big company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家大公司从事人力资源管理工作。
words.en: Human resources management involves the strategic approach to the effective and efficient management of people in a company or organization such that they help their business gain a competitive advantage.

words.ex: He is learning marketing management at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习市场营销管理。
words.en: Marketing management is the organizational discipline which focuses on the practical application of marketing orientation, techniques and methods inside enterprises and organizations and on the management of a firm's marketing resources and activities.

words.tr: phrase. 战略营销；指企业为实现长期目标而制定并执行的市场规划与竞争策略
words.ex: He uses strategic marketing to sell more products.
words.ex_cn: 他使用战略营销来销售更多产品。
words.en: Strategic marketing involves the identification of the most profitable market segments and the development of marketing strategies to serve those segments effectively.

words.tr: phrase. 制造与生产；制造业与生产活动
words.ex: The factory focuses on manufacturing and production of cars.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂专注于汽车的制造和生产。
words.en: The sector of the economy involved in the creation of goods through the use of machinery, tools, and labor, encompassing both the making and assembly of products.

words.tr: phrase. 运营管理；运营管理学（研究如何有效规划、组织、指挥和控制生产与服务运营过程的学科）
words.ex: He works in operations management at a factory.
words.ex_cn: 他在工厂从事运营管理。
words.en: Operations management is the area of management concerned with designing and controlling the process of production and redesigning business operations in the production of goods or services.

words.ex: The statistics show a rise in sales last year.
words.ex_cn: 这些统计数字显示去年销售额有所上升。
words.en: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data.

words.tr: phrase. 技术与信息系统（指用于数据处理、存储和通信的软硬件综合体系）
words.ex: He works with technology and information systems at his company.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司里使用技术和信息系统。
words.en: The field that involves the use of digital tools, software, and networks to manage, process, and disseminate information, crucial for modern business operations.

words.ex: He works in a company that uses a management information system.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家使用管理信息系统公司工作。
words.en: A management information system (MIS) is an organized system that gathers, stores, and disseminates information in the form of reports and other outputs to support decision-making in an organization.

words.tr: abbr. 管理信息系统；“management information system”的缩写
words.ex: He misread the instructions and made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他误读了说明，犯了一个错误。
words.en: A title used before the surname or full name of an unmarried woman or girl.

words.ex: He is learning microeconomics this semester.
words.ex_cn: 他这学期正在学习微观经济学。
words.en: Microeconomics is the part of economics concerned with single factors and the effects of individual decisions.

words.ex: He is learning macroeconomics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习宏观经济学。
words.en: Macroeconomics is the branch of economics concerned with large-scale or general economic factors, such as interest rates and national productivity.

words.ex: The new policy is for the promotion of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策是为了促进清洁能源。
words.en: A promotion is a move to a more important job or rank in a company or organization.

words.ex: The doctor checked his daily intake of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他每天的糖摄入量。
words.en: The process of taking something in, especially food, air, or information.

words.tr:
n. 踪迹；轨道；小路；跑道；
v. 追踪；跟踪；
words.ex: The dog followed the track of the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 狗跟着兔子的踪迹。
words.en: A track is a path or route along which something moves or travels. It can also refer to marks left by something that has passed, or the act of following such marks to find someone or something.

words.ex: The school changed its curriculum last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年学校更改了课程。
words.en: A curriculum is the subjects that are studied in a school, college, or university.

words.tr: adj. 强制性的；义务的；必须的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is obligatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制性的。
words.en: If something is obligatory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: adj. 强制的；法定的；义务的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is mandatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制的。
words.en: If something is mandatory, it is required by law or by a rule or regulation.

words.tr: adj. 可选择的；非强制的；
words.ex: The field trip is optional.
words.ex_cn: 这次郊游是可选的。
words.en: If something is optional, you can choose whether or not you do it or have it.

words.tr:
adj. 选举的；选修的；可选择的
n. 选修课程
words.ex: He voted in the elective process for mayor.
